questions.question: What is the difference between comics and graphic novels?
options: Comics are usually short and serialised; graphic novels are longer, complete stories often in book format
Comics have pictures; graphic novels have only text
Comics are for adults; graphic novels are for children
There is no difference at all
questions.explanation: Comics are short serialised stories in newspapers and magazines, while graphic novels are longer, coherent narratives, often dealing with deeper themes.

questions.question: What is the graphic novel "Maus" by Art Spiegelman about?
options: The Holocaust, told with animal characters
A superhero in New York
A lazy cat who loves lasagne
Growing up in Iran
questions.explanation: "Maus" tells a Holocaust story using animals - it is one of the most acclaimed graphic novels and won the Pulitzer Prize. "Persepolis" is about growing up in Iran.

questions.question: In comics, what does a large panel usually signal?
options: An important moment
A fast, unimportant event
The end of the story
A printing error
questions.explanation: Panel size matters: large panels highlight important moments, while small panels often show quick events.

questions.question: How can colour be used as a visual device in comics?
options: Dark colours can show danger or sadness; bright colours can show joy
Colour has no meaning in comics
Colours only show the time of day
Dark colours always mean the story is over
questions.explanation: Colour creates mood: dark colours can signal danger or sadness, while bright colours can signal happiness.

questions.question: How do comics usually show what a character thinks (rather than says)?
options: With a thought bubble
With a speech bubble
With a caption box only
Thoughts cannot be shown in comics
questions.explanation: Thought bubbles (usually cloud-shaped) show what characters think, while speech bubbles show what they say aloud.
